items.title: PREVENT post hoc: fewer events with preventive PCI seen only in NIRS-defined lipid-rich plaques
items.summary: Circulation post hoc analysis of PREVENT (598 patients, 632 non-flow-limiting lesions with plaque burden >70% and MLA <4 mm² on IVUS plus NIRS): preventive PCI was associated with fewer primary-outcome events only in lipid-rich plaques (7% vs 18%), with no benefit in non-lipid-rich plaques despite similar anatomy.
bullets: **PREVENT post hoc analysis** (Circulation, 6 Oct 2026): does **plaque composition** decide who benefits from **preventive PCI**?
Parent trial: **1,606 patients**, 15 centres in Asia and New Zealand. This analysis: **598 patients, 632 lesions** (plaque burden >70%, MLA <4 mm² on IVUS) also imaged with **NIRS**.
**Lipid-rich plaque (LRP)** = max lipid core burden index over 4 mm **>315**; present in **223 patients (37%)**.
Median follow-up **5.6 years**: events were **more frequent with LRP (13% vs 5%; HR 2.08)**.
**With LRP**, preventive PCI + OMT vs OMT alone: **7% vs 18%** (adjusted **HR 0.23**, p<0.001).
Caveat: **post hoc** subgroup of an open-label trial; the authors call for **prospective NIRS-guided** trials.

items.title: AI-enhanced auscultation detects LVEF ≤40% with AUROC 0.90 on external validation (NEJM AI)
items.summary: Prospective multicentre Japanese study (NEJM AI, Oct 15): an AI model analysing digital-stethoscope recordings from four auscultation sites detected LV dysfunction (LVEF ≤40%) with AUROC 0.904 in external validation and beat cardiologist consensus in a reader substudy. Proposed as a pre-echo triage tool, not yet for screening.
bullets: **NEJM AI** prospective multicentre study: **AI auscultation** to detect **LV dysfunction (LVEF ≤40%)** before echo.
Digital stethoscope recordings at **four sites** plus a **single-lead ECG**; an ensemble of a transformer and a 1D-CNN.
**Training**: 2,359 patients (8.9% with reduced LVEF). **External validation**: 964 patients (7.6% reduced LVEF).
In a **100-patient reader substudy**, AI beat **cardiologist consensus** on accuracy: **82.0% vs 62.0%** (p=0.004).
A **two-site** version kept **AUROC 0.903**; the AI outperformed ECG-only and clinical-variable/BNP models.
Caveats: for **pre-echo risk enrichment** in referred patients, not screening; **industry-funded** (AMI Inc.); needs more validation.
